title: Project Overview
description: Start with README.md to learn what Ivy Engine is: a from-scratch C++ / Direct3D 11 engine with an ImGui editor, physics, a job system, C++ DLL scripting, and one-click deploy. The document also covers Visual Studio 2022 build steps and points to the deeper engine manuals, so it is the map for the tour ahead.

title: Engine Versus Content
description: Ivy Engine keeps the engine repo separate from game content. CONTEXT.md defines the preferred names for content projects, deploy packages, cameras, and visuals, while CONTENT_PROJECT.md explains the external_content_template starter a game repo should own. The in-repo project.json is a sample content-project file: game name, default scene, and editor zoom, showing that a game is project.json plus rom/ plus GameScripts.dll, not a fork of the engine.

title: Dual Application Hosts
description: Building on that split, the engine ships two Win32 hosts from one solution. IvyEngine.sln builds the ImGui editor (IvyEngine.exe) and the deploy host (IvyEngineRuntime.exe) for Debug/Release on x64 and Win32. src/app/main.cpp is the shared Windows entry: it creates a DPI-aware window, initializes renderer, input, audio, and jobs, then runs a 60 Hz update/draw loop. IvyEngineRuntime.vcxproj compiles the GAME_RUNTIME play host that uses the same scene loop without the editor UI.

title: Shared GameScene Loop
description: Both hosts hand control to GameScene, the playable SceneBase that owns initialize, update, and draw plus per-pass render-object selection. game_scene.cpp implements the play/edit loop: boot preload, shadow and lighting setup, parallel player Update with snapshot/flushes, then cascaded-shadow and post-process draw. SceneManager is the singleton that swaps SceneBase instances, clears physics trigger pairs, and forwards Update and Draw, so editor and runtime share one scene lifetime.

title: Host-Initialized Core Services
description: Following main.cpp outward, three high-fan-in headers are the services the host loop depends on. engine_gui.h is the public editor/runtime GUI API for play mode, scene load/save, camera mode, and viewport mapping. renderer.h is the Direct3D 11 surface: device accessors, material and vertex layouts, viewports, and post-process render targets. job_system.h is the frame-level scheduler used later by GameScene for parallel player updates, with submit, dependency fences, and a parallel toggle.

title: ECS Scene Nodes
description: The scene loop ticks GameObjects, the highest-fan-in type in the graph. game_object.h is the core scene node: a typed component map, parent/child hierarchy, legacy pose fields, and collider factories. Component is the base interface with owner pointer, lifecycle hooks, parameter injection, and JSON serialize/deserialize. SceneTransform stores local pose, world-matrix helpers, and the start-state snapshot Return-to-Start uses when play mode stops.
languageLesson: This ECS is component-map based rather than a packed archetype store: each GameObject owns typed components that implement a shared lifecycle and JSON contract, so editor save, play-mode spawn, and scripts all talk to the same node type.

title: Scene Load Pipeline
description: SceneLoader turns ROM JSON into the GameObject trees from Step 6. It initializes and finalizes the scene system, loads and saves JSON, registers ECS component types, hot-reloads script DLLs, and tears down play sessions. rom/scene/default_scene.txt is a one-line startup pointer naming scene_sample_menu.json, the sample title-menu scene with skybox, lighting, and UI buttons that load playground or PBR scenes or quit.
languageLesson: Scene files are JSON documents, not compiled binaries: loaders register component types then deserialize each node, so a missing component type or a renamed field shows up as a load failure rather than a silent skip.

title: Play Versus Edit
description: The same GameObject scene is driven two ways. engine_gui.cpp is the ImGui editor shell that owns hierarchy, inspector, play-mode sessions, project workflows, and viewport picking. engine_gui_runtime.cpp is the non-editor EngineGUI: it starts play, ticks non-player scene nodes, and stubs editor-only UI hooks so IvyEngineRuntime.exe can ship without ImGui panels. SceneRuntime syncs editor roots into the active SceneBase for physics and applies or clears collider components when play starts or stops.

title: GameScripts DLL
description: Gameplay lives in a hot-reload GameScripts.dll, not in the engine hosts. Script.h is the user script base with create/update/destroy, trigger callbacks, and JSON hooks. script_runtime_api.h is the host function-pointer table and ScriptApi_* wrappers that expose input, cameras, UI, particles, physics, audio, and scene services to that DLL. ContentProject.sln is the Visual Studio template that builds the DLL, and game_scene_script_hooks.cpp resolves optional hook exports on the loaded module, treating a missing bool hook as success.
languageLesson: The engine talks to content through a versioned C function-pointer table rather than C++ classes across the DLL boundary. That keeps ABI stable when GameScripts.dll hot-reloads: the host fills ScriptRuntimeApi, and scripts call ScriptApi_* wrappers instead of linking engine internals.

title: Direct3D 11 Rendering
description: GameScene's draw path goes through the D3D11 shader API in shader.h: standard, toon, and PBR 3D variants, a skinning palette, SurfaceFX params, and cascaded-shadow matrix binds. LightingCommon.hlsli is the shared HLSL lighting library for shadows, hemisphere ambient, classic lights, toon bands, height fog, and Cook-Torrance PBR. PixelShader3D_PBR.hlsl is the Cook-Torrance pixel shader that lights all types with roughness, metallic, and a Fresnel-boosted ambient term.
languageLesson: HLSL .hlsli files are include libraries, not entry-point programs. Shared lighting math lives in LightingCommon.hlsli so PBR, toon, and classic pixel shaders stay consistent, while each .hlsl file provides a single vertex or pixel entry point compiled to a .cso.

title: Physics Simulation
description: Play mode from Step 8 also ticks physics. physics_system.cpp snapshots positions, integrates gravity, runs a swept broad phase, fires trigger enter/exit, and exposes raycasts used by scripts and scene changes. collider.cpp implements box, sphere, capsule, cylinder, and mesh colliders with world poses, contact generation, and debug wireframes. ColliderComponent is the ECS side: serialized shape settings that apply to or clear a GameObject physics collider when SceneRuntime registers the tree.

title: ImGui Editor Tools
description: The editor host from Step 3 is more than the EngineGUI shell. ProjectManager opens Unity-style content projects (project.json, rom/, game/scripts), tracks recents, and stores editor, physics, and audio settings. editor_undo.h defines the undo command interface and stack for transform, component, and canvas edits so play-mode Return-to-Start is not the only revert path. The project-browser panel lets the ImGui editor pick and spawn assets from the open content project.

title: Playable Package Deploy
description: Shipping closes the engine-versus-content split from Step 2. playable_package_builder.cpp is the editor pipeline that finds MSBuild, compiles the content project, and copies a playable game package to a user destination. ADR 0002 defines File → Build Current Project as that full package: MSBuild of IvyEngineRuntime and GameScripts, then staging of the renamed host, DLLs, project.json, rom, and current .cso shader overlays, so a content project can run without the editor.
